data.narrative:
Deep Sentinel, a Series B-stage defense and security company founded by David Selinger, has raised $55M to date. The valuation analysis employs two primary methods triangulated against a comp universe of 10 peers: 8 private companies and 2 public equities (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) in the same sector and stage.

The stage-progression method applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical for Series B progression, yielding $104.5M based on $55M total raised as a proxy. The peer-median approach references 8 same-sector, same-stage private companies—Dream Security ($3.0B), Allen Control Systems ($2.2B), Harmattan AI ($1.4B), Code Metal ($1.2B), and Twenty ($1.0B) among others—which establish a median valuation of $1.1B with a range of $300M to $3.0B. These peers exhibit substantial dispersion, reflecting variance in revenue traction or customer concentration within Defense & Security.

The two-method triangulation supports a valuation range of $89M (low) to $1.3B (high), with a median of $615M. The wide spread reflects material uncertainty: stage-progression methods tend to underweight market-comparables valuation, while peer-median valuations assume Deep Sentinel's market position and defensibility align with higher-valued comps. Capital efficiency, customer retention, and competitive differentiation remain critical discriminators within this range.
